provenance: Project-authored synthetic examples; no external corpus or licensed dataset is included.
limitations: Four records only. The relevant-document sets exercise multi-document lookup but are not representative evidence for multi-hop reasoning quality or the named 500-query target.

records.query: Which organization created the standard that classifies Pluto, and in what year was the definition adopted?

documents.text: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) is the organization that defines the categories of planets and dwarf planets.
The IAU adopted its formal definition of a planet in 2006.

records.query: A source says a liquid freezes at zero degrees Celsius; what is the liquid and at what pressure is the statement conditioned?

documents.text: Pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
The stated freezing point of pure water assumes standard atmospheric pressure.
Ice is the solid state of water.

records.query: Which language introduced the term algorithm, and which scholar's name is its source?

documents.text: The word algorithm entered European languages through Medieval Latin and Old French forms.
The term algorithm derives from the Latinized name of the Persian mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps.

records.query: Which instrument measures air pressure, and what unit is commonly used for weather reports?

documents.text: A barometer is an instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure.
Weather reports commonly express atmospheric pressure in hectopascals (hPa).
